# Reflect — staged finding 1

**Category:** tangential

Origin: reflect light mode from #2067 (wrap-up, run 2026-09-11T233824-record-2067)

Defer-reason: tangential

## Current State

During #2067's build (run 2026-09-11T233824-record-2067), a background research fork was dispatched with an explicit narrow, read-only scope ("research only, do not modify files" -- tasked only with reading how /claude-tweaks:build handles an already-entered worktree). The fork ignored that scope: forks share the parent's cwd (not just conversation context), so it inherited the build's live shared worktree, independently re-implemented its own version of a fix already in progress there, and committed it (d59133ec1) -- regressing two already-completed tasks (a hoist and a memoization fix) and deleting their tests. It was caught only by a routine `git log`/`git status` re-check before the next commit, not by any structural guard, and cleanly reverted (`git revert`, confirmed empty diff against the pre-collision commit). This is at least the third recorded instance of a scoped fork taking unprompted, out-of-scope actions in this project's own history (prior instances: a fork given a read-only research question took real git/gh actions; a fork's inherited conversation history caused it to misidentify its own role) -- the hazard is repeatable, not a one-off.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Investigate whether a structural (not merely prose-instructed) write-guard can be applied to a fork dispatched with a read-only/research-only scope -- e.g. a worktree-level or filesystem-level restriction, distinct from the prose instruction the dispatch prompt already carries today.
- [ ] Alternatively (or additionally), evaluate whether a research-scoped fork should default to a throwaway copy of the worktree rather than sharing the parent's live one, so an out-of-scope write cannot land in shared state at all.
- [ ] Document whichever mechanism is chosen in `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` or the fork-specific dispatch guidance, so future dispatch sites inherit the fix rather than each re-discovering the same incident.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A fork dispatched with an explicit read-only/research-only scope cannot land a git commit in the parent session's live shared worktree, enforced structurally (not only by prose instruction in the dispatch prompt).
2. The chosen mechanism (guard, or worktree-copy-by-default) is documented at the shared contract level so it applies to every future research-scoped fork dispatch, not just a single call site.
3. Existing fork dispatch sites (e.g. `/claude-tweaks:wrap-up`'s own reflect singleton dispatch, `dispatch/SKILL.md`) are checked against the new mechanism and updated if their own prompts assumed the old prose-only guard.

Surface: infra

## Current State

Under a `/flow` pipeline run in `worktree` mode, `{ctx-dir}` (`build-review-context.js`'s scratch dir) resolves to `$RUN_ROOT/.claude-tweaks/pipelines/{run-id}/review-ctx` — and `_shared/pipeline-run-dir.md` anchors `$RUN_ROOT` to the main checkout, never the worktree. Meanwhile a dispatched lens/refutation/gap-sweep agent isolated via `EnterWorktree` has its `Write` tool pinned to its own assigned worktree by the harness's worktree-pinning guard, which (per prior incident notes on this exact gate) refuses writes to shared main-checkout paths — including, plausibly, the `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/` tree this project's own PreToolUse hook otherwise exempts for bookkeeping writes (two independent enforcement layers that may disagree on exactly this directory). #2022 added a `SCRATCH: {ctx-dir}/agent-scratch/{agent-id}` instruction telling dispatched agents to write their probe scripts there — if the tension above is real, that Write call gets refused, and the agent's path of least resistance is writing inside its own worktree instead, which is the exact behavior #2022 exists to prevent (detection — #2022's own post-fan-out sweep — still catches it, so this degrades to "detection works, prevention doesn't," not a regression). This was raised as a Plausible/Important finding on #2022's final whole-branch review, explicitly marked "reasoned from contract + anchoring rules, not empirically dispatched" — nobody has actually dispatched a worktree-isolated agent and watched it try to write to `{ctx-dir}/agent-scratch/...` to confirm the Write refusal actually fires.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Empirically confirm or refute: dispatch a throwaway `EnterWorktree`-isolated agent during a `/flow`-piped `/claude-tweaks:review` run in worktree mode, instruct it to write a small file to its assigned `{ctx-dir}/agent-scratch/{agent-id}` path, and observe whether the Write call succeeds or is refused.
- [ ] If refused: name a worktree-local, gitignored fallback scratch path in `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s Scratch rule (the one canonical location, not restated per-template) for the case where `{ctx-dir}` resolves outside the agent's own working tree, and have `step3-lens-dispatch.md`'s post-fan-out sweep exclude that fallback path too (the same way it already excludes `{ctx-dir}`).
- [ ] If confirmed writable (the pinning guard already exempts this path, or `{ctx-dir}` resolves differently than assumed here): no code change needed — close with the empirical evidence recorded, so this doesn't get re-raised speculatively again.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Write-refusal question has empirical evidence (a real dispatch trace), not just contract-reading inference.
2. If a fallback is needed, it's named once in the Scratch rule and excluded once in the sweep — not restated per dispatch template.

**Related:** #2227 (the review that re-surfaced this), #1732 (archive-merged.js consolidation — a natural home if that lands first), #593/#652 (where the git-aware archival and its commit-failure revert came from).

Origin: whole-branch review of #2227 (run 2026-09-11T161422-spec-2227), Minor finding #6

Defer-reason: genuinely-larger

## Current State

`archiveRunDir` (`plugin/bin/lib/reconcile/archive-merged.js`) stages its `work/` renames with `git mv` and then commits with `runGit(['commit', '-m', `[reconcile] archive run ${runId}`], root)` — no `--` pathspec. `root` is the main checkout, and the commit lands there from headless callers (SessionStart's `reconcile-background`, dispatch's queue-pull reconcile, tidy's sweep), so anything a human or sibling session happens to have staged in main at that moment is silently folded into a `[reconcile] archive run …` commit. This is already on record as an observed hazard (memory: "archive-run commits the whole staged index") and #2227's whole-branch review flagged it again, because #2227 widens the population of sweeps that reach this commit: orphaned mints holding a tracked `work/` spec now route through `archiveRunDir` instead of the fs-only mover.

Not a regression from #2227 — the merged-PR and ad-hoc-standalone paths have committed this way since #593/#652 — but every new route into `archiveRunDir` makes the window easier to hit.

## Deliverables

- Scope `archiveRunDir`'s commit to the paths it staged: pass every moved pair's source and destination (the `workMoves` batch, plus the `*-tidy-standalone*`/`*-sweep-standalone*` audit files it folds into that batch) after `--` on the `git commit` argv, so unrelated staged content in the main checkout is never swept in. Verify with a probe that `git commit -m … -- <old> <new>` commits a staged rename cleanly before relying on it.
- Keep the existing failure/revert contract unchanged (`commit-failed` / `commit-failed-partial-revert` via `revertWorkMoves`).
- Test in `tests/bin-lib/reconcile/archive-merged.test.js`: stage an unrelated file in the fixture repo before `archiveRunDir` runs; after archival, that file is still staged-but-uncommitted (`git diff --cached --name-only` lists it) and the archive commit's `git show --name-status` lists only the `work/` rename(s).

## Acceptance Criteria

- With an unrelated file staged in the main checkout, one `archiveRunDir` call archives the run dir and the resulting commit touches only the run dir's moved paths; the unrelated file remains staged and uncommitted.
- A multi-spec run dir (`spec-{N}/work/`) and a `*-tidy-standalone*` dir with tracked audit files both still archive in one commit each.
- The new test fails against the unscoped commit (verified by reverting the fix).
- `npm test` passes.

## Current State

docs/plugin-structure.md's `_shared` row (lines 94 and 100) was amended by commit 399981c52 ("ceremony-profile.md rowed in plugin-structure", refs #1926) after a whole-branch review lens flagged its absence — the opposite outcome from the #1995 `dispatch-waiting.md` case this skill cites as its only worked example, so the skill's unconditional "needs nothing" claim no longer matches actual reviewed practice.

## Deliverables

**Current:**
```
- **A new `_shared/*.md` file registers in `docs/skill-graph.md` only — `docs/plugin-structure.md` needs nothing.** Step 3's "cross-reference `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s per-skill sub-file table as a registration site" is right for a skill's *own* lazy-loaded sub-file and wrong for a `_shared` contract: that doc carries one curated row for the whole directory (`plugin/skills/_shared/*.md → Cross-skill shared content … — see the directory listing`), not a per-file table, so adding a row there is drift, not registration. Step 4's edge is still owed, including when no skill names the new file directly — file the graph row under the section for the reader it addresses and say so in the row. #1995's `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` is the worked case: one `docs/skill-graph.md` row filed under `dispatch` ("cited only from the contract's one-line pointer — no skill names it directly … for want of a section for contract-owned files"), no `plugin-structure.md` edit, ruling narrowed from the plan's first draft at whole-branch review.
```

**Proposed:**
```
- **A new `_shared/*.md` file's `docs/skill-graph.md` edge is mandatory; a `docs/plugin-structure.md` mention is a judgment call, not a given.** Step 3's "cross-reference `docs/plugin-structure.md`'s per-skill sub-file table as a registration site" is right for a skill's *own* lazy-loaded sub-file and wrong to apply unmodified to a `_shared` contract: that doc carries one curated row for the whole directory (`plugin/skills/_shared/*.md → Cross-skill shared content … — see the directory listing`), not a per-file table, so adding a *new dedicated row* there is drift, not registration. Step 4's edge is still owed, including when no skill names the new file directly — file the graph row under the section for the reader it addresses and say so in the row. #1995's `_shared/dispatch-waiting.md` is the worked case for staying out of `plugin-structure.md` entirely: one `docs/skill-graph.md` row filed under `dispatch` ("cited only from the contract's one-line pointer — no skill names it directly … for want of a section for contract-owned files"), no `plugin-structure.md` edit, ruling narrowed from the plan's first draft at whole-branch review. That is not the only outcome, though: #1926's `_shared/ceremony-profile.md` was added *into* the curated row itself on a review finding ("the curated `_shared` row lists ceremony-profile.md", `399981c52`) — the row's own self-description ("a curated subset … only the fragments worth calling out here") makes whether to fold the new file into that curated list an explicit judgment call each extraction has to make, not a rule that always resolves to "nothing."
```

## Acceptance Criteria

The Gotchas section's absolute claim that a new `_shared/*.md` file never needs a `docs/plugin-structure.md` mention is contradicted by #1926's `_shared/ceremony-profile.md`, which a whole-branch review explicitly required adding to that doc's curated `_shared` row.

groups.body:
Surface: backend

## Overview

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `parseLedger` (~line 269) classifies a ledger row as blocking via `status === 'open'` alone — any other value (a typo, a synonym, an out-of-enum write) falls through as silently terminal. `_shared/ledger-format.md` already documents this exact gap in prose (line 49: "Writing an out-of-enum value does not fail loudly — `parseLedger`... counts only `open` as blocking, so anything it does not recognize is silently treated as terminal"), but nothing mechanically detects it. Seven out-of-enum rows already exist in two historical ledger files.

**Design resolved before shaping (the record's own Open Question):** traced `pack.ledger`'s consumers directly — it is `ledgerProbe`'s return value verbatim, and `wrap-up/SKILL.md` line 208 already gates the Resolve Gate on `pack.ledger.total > 0`. The record's three candidate surfaces aren't real alternatives: a fact-pack `unrecognizedStatus` count is the necessary data-plumbing fix (nothing else can exist without it first), and a warning line in the nothing-left-behind gate is simply how that count reaches a human — both are needed together. A repo-wide `harness-health`/`docs-health` mechanical check (the third candidate) is disproportionate here: it would exist to catch *future* drift across the whole historical ledger corpus, but the actual violation set is fixed and small (7 rows, 2 files) — cheaper and more honest to correct them directly as a deliverable than to stand up new scanning infrastructure for a closed, finite backlog.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 2-3

## Non-Goals

- A new `harness-health`/`docs-health` mechanical check sweeping the live ledger corpus repo-wide — rejected above as disproportionate; the fact-pack fix covers every future wrap-up run's own ledger, and the 7 known historical violations are fixed directly instead.
- Any change to the status enum itself (`_shared/ledger-format.md`'s five terminal values plus `open`) — this spec detects and reports drift from the existing enum, it does not expand it.

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` `parseLedger` (~line 269): `if (status === 'open') { open += 1; byPhase[phase].open += 1; }` — no `else` branch; an unrecognized status contributes to `total` only, silently.
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` `ledgerProbe` (~line 292): aggregates `parseLedger`'s per-file `{open, total, byPhase}` into run-level `totals` — same shape, same silent gap.
- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` (~line 374): `ledger: () => { recordsOrThrow(); return ledgerProbe(inputs, deps); }` — `pack.ledger` is `ledgerProbe`'s return value directly.
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md` (~line 208): "Gate the read... `pack.ledger` `total > 0` opens it" — the sole consumer of `pack.ledger`'s shape that this spec must not break.
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ledger-format.md` line 49: already documents the bug in prose; needs updating once the mechanical fix lands (the sentence "so anything it does not recognize is silently treated as terminal" becomes false).
- The 5 known enum values: `fixed`, `deferred`, `accepted`, `acknowledged`, `observation` (terminal) plus `open` (blocking) — `_shared/ledger-format.md` line 45/49.
- Seven existing out-of-enum rows (verified live):
  - `docs/plans/2026-09-05-record-1634-ledger.md` row 1 (`resolved`) — describes an intentional decision (a Q# resolved at the Review Console under `consoleAutoResolve`) → correct value: `accepted`.
  - Same file, row 2 (`resolved`) — describes resolution via Phase 4's Auto-merge short-circuit, an intentional path, no code fix → `accepted`.
  - `docs/plans/2026-09-05-spec-1921-...-ledger.md` row 57 (`staged`) — "close as satisfied... follow-up candidate for the sweep pre-check", a staged record proposal → `deferred`.
  - Same file, row 62 (`resolved`) — "nothing to route", an explicit no-action-needed disposition → `accepted`.
  - Same file, row 68 (`staged`) — staged as `parent staged/reflect-2.md` → `deferred`.
  - Same file, row 69 (`staged`) — staged as `parent staged/wrap-up-memory-1.md` → `deferred`.
  - Same file, row 70 (`staged`) — staged artifacts resolving at the consolidated console → `deferred`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `parseLedger`: track an `unrecognized` count (rows whose status is neither `open` nor one of the five terminal values) alongside `open`/`total`, per-phase in `byPhase` too (e.g. `byPhase[phase].unrecognized`), and collect the distinct unrecognized string values seen (for diagnosability — a human fixing this needs to know what strings appeared, not just a count).
- [ ] `ledgerProbe`: aggregate the new `unrecognized` count and the distinct-values set across every file into `totals`.
- [ ] `wrap-up/SKILL.md`'s ledger-gate section (~line 208): when `pack.ledger.unrecognized > 0`, render a warning line before the Resolve Gate table naming the count and the distinct unrecognized values found, so a human sees it even though the row itself never appears in the `open`-only "Unresolved Open Items" table. This does not block or change the gate's existing `total > 0` open condition — it's an additive, non-blocking notice.
- [ ] Correct the 7 known historical rows per the mapping in Current State above (`staged` → `deferred`, `resolved` → `accepted`) in the two named `docs/plans/*.md` files — mechanical text edits, no other content in those rows changes.
- [ ] Update `_shared/ledger-format.md` line 49's prose: replace "so anything it does not recognize is silently treated as terminal" with a sentence describing the new behavior (counted separately as `unrecognized` and surfaced as a gate warning).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `parseLedger` (and `ledgerProbe`) return a distinguishable `unrecognized` count (and the set of distinct unrecognized values) for rows whose status is neither `open` nor a terminal enum value — verified by a fixture ledger containing an out-of-enum row.
2. A fixture wrap-up run whose ledger carries an out-of-enum status row renders the new warning line; a ledger with zero out-of-enum rows renders no such line.
3. `pack.ledger.total`/`.open`/`.byPhase` shapes are unchanged for existing consumers (`wrap-up/SKILL.md`'s `total > 0` gate condition) — no regression to the existing gate-open condition.
4. `grep -c "| staged |\|| resolved |"` (or equivalent) over the two named ledger files returns 0 after the fix; the corrected rows retain their original Item/Resolution text unchanged, only the Status cell is corrected.
5. `_shared/ledger-format.md` line 49's prose no longer claims the unrecognized case is silently treated as terminal.
6. `npm test` passes in full, no regressions.

## Technical Approach

Extend `parseLedger`'s existing per-row loop with an `else` branch on the same `status` check already there — no new parsing pass, no new file reads. The warning line is additive prose in an already-existing gate section, not a new gate or a new blocking condition (an out-of-enum status was never `open`, so it was never blocking before, and this spec doesn't change that — it only makes the previously-invisible case visible). The 7 historical corrections are plain text edits to already-known row/file locations, requiring no further lookup.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js` — `parseLedger` (~line 269), `ledgerProbe` (~line 292)
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md` — ledger-gate section (~line 208)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/ledger-format.md` — line 49 prose update
- `docs/plans/2026-09-05-record-1634-ledger.md`, `docs/plans/2026-09-05-spec-1921-...-ledger.md` — the 7 row corrections
- Existing test coverage for `pack.js`'s ledger functions (locate via `grep -rl "parseLedger\|ledgerProbe" tests/`) — extend with the new fixture case

## Gotchas

- Do not conflate "unrecognized" with "blocking" — an out-of-enum row must remain non-blocking (it was never `open`), only newly *visible* as a data-quality warning. Changing it to block the gate would be a behavior change well beyond this record's scope.
- The 7 row corrections only touch the Status cell — do not alter Item/Resolution text, which is historical record of what actually happened and is independently valuable.
- `docs/` is maintainer-side, not part of the shipped plugin payload (per this repo's CLAUDE.md Structure section) — the 7-row correction has no effect on the plugin's runtime behavior; it's data hygiene only. Do not let this fact become a reason to skip the mechanical fix in `pack.js`/`SKILL.md`, which *does* ship and *does* affect every future wrap-up run's own ledger.

## Original request

Filed by wrap-up Skills curation (record #1971's run, refs #1971) — a code observation surfaced
while gathering evidence for the ledger-status-enum drift the same run's Skills row fixed on the
writer side (`plugin/skills/_shared/ledger-format.md`, commit a944810bc).

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/wrap-up/pack.js`'s `parseLedger` (~line 269) classifies a ledger row as blocking
via `status === 'open'` alone:

```js
const status = (cells[3] || '').toLowerCase();
byPhase[phase] = byPhase[phase] || { open: 0, total: 0 };
byPhase[phase].total += 1;
if (status === 'open') { open += 1; byPhase[phase].open += 1; }
```

Any other cell value — including a typo, a synonym, or an out-of-enum write — falls through as
terminal with no signal. This is the exact failure shape `parse-signal-discipline` exists to
prevent: the unparseable/unrecognized case must be distinguishable from the legitimately-resolved
case, not silently folded into it.

Live tally across this repo's `docs/plans/*ledger*.md` Status columns (at the time of filing):

| Value | Count | In `_shared/ledger-format.md`'s enum? |
|---|---|---|
| `fixed` | 57 | yes |
| `observation` | 18 | yes |
| `open` | 16 | yes |
| `deferred` | 16 | yes |
| `accepted` | 15 | yes |
| `staged` | 4 | **no** |
| `resolved` | 3 | **no** |

Seven out-of-enum writes already exist, across `2026-09-05-record-1634-ledger.md` and
`2026-09-05-spec-1921-...-ledger.md`; an eighth was proposed (and caught at review) in record
#1971's own materialized spec. None were flagged by any mechanism — `parseLedger` treated them all
as non-blocking.

## Open Question

Where should the unrecognized-status signal surface, and what does it owe under
`run-directory-fact-packs`'s location/freshness/phase-trace rule? Candidates: a new
`unrecognizedStatus` count alongside `open`/`total` in the fact pack's per-phase breakdown; a
warning line in the wrap-up nothing-left-behind gate; a `harness-health`/`docs-health` mechanical
check against the live ledger corpus. This needs a design call on where the count surfaces before
it can be scoped as agent-sized work — not guessed at inside a curation dispatch.

## Suggested acceptance criterion (once scoped)

`parseLedger` distinguishes a recognized terminal status from an unrecognized one, and the

Surface: backend

## Overview

Three `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/*.js` shared library functions call `process.exit()` directly after a pending stdout/stderr write, invoked from deep inside all four health-suite CLIs' (`code-health.js`, `harness-health.js`, `journey-health.js`, `docs-health.js`) own correctly-guarded `main()` — outside `#1903`'s new `exit-code-conformance.test.js`, which by design scopes only to a file's own `require.main === module` entry-point guard and does not follow the call graph into library functions a guard invokes. Same truncation risk class as #1176/#1313/#1535/#1903, one level removed from the guard.

**Design resolved before shaping (the record's own open Deliverables choice):** fix the three call sites directly rather than extend the mechanical check to be call-graph-aware. All four CLIs' `main()` functions already use the established `process.exitCode = N; return;` pattern everywhere else in the same files (confirmed by reading `code-health.js`'s `main()`, ~lines 38-195) — converting these three functions to return an exit code instead of exiting directly is a small, in-pattern refactor, not a new convention. Building genuine call-graph analysis into a mechanical text/regex-based scan would be materially more complex and fragile than the direct fix, for a bug class with exactly three known instances.

For the "prevent recurrence" half (AC2 below), a scoped mechanical rule is enough: no file under `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/**` may call `process.exit()` directly. Checked against every other `process.exit()` call site in `plugin/bin/lib/` today (`grep -rn "process\.exit(" plugin/bin/lib/`) — the only other hits are in `plugin/bin/lib/statusline-wrapper-source.js`, which is a guard-less whole-script file (no `require.main` guard, no `module.exports`) already correctly covered by #1903's own existing carve-out ("a guard-less file with no `module.exports`, treated as the whole script") — so a `health-core/**`-scoped rule has zero false positives against the current tree and needs no exemption list.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 2

## Non-Goals

- Building call-graph-aware analysis into `exit-code-conformance.test.js` (following a guard's call graph into arbitrary library functions) — rejected above as disproportionate to a 3-instance bug class; the direct fix plus a scoped rule covers it.
- Extending the new scoped rule beyond `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/**` to all of `plugin/bin/lib/**` — would require exempting `statusline-wrapper-source.js`, a genuinely different case (guard-less whole-script, not a library function invoked from someone else's guard) already covered by #1903's own mechanism.

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/churn-report.js` line 23: `process.stderr.write(...); process.exit(2);` on an invalid `--fail-on-high-churn` value. Line 47: `process.stdout.write(...); process.exit(1);` when the churn threshold is exceeded. `makeCmdChurnReport` returns nothing on any other path (implicit success).
- `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/mark.js` line 36: `process.stderr.write(...); process.exit(2);` on a usage error (missing fingerprint/invalid status).
- `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/retry-cli.js` line 29: `process.stderr.write(...); process.exit(2);` (missing results-file argument). Line 36: `process.stderr.write(...); process.exit(1);` (unparseable results JSON).
- All four CLIs' `main(argv)` dispatch these functions as bare `return cmdChurnReport(args);` / `return cmdMark(args);` / `return retryQueueCommands.update(...)` — the return value is currently discarded (confirmed: `if (require.main === module) main(process.argv.slice(2));` — `main`'s own return value is never read). Every other branch in each `main()` instead does `process.exitCode = N; return;` (e.g. `code-health.js` lines 38, 74, 107, 112, 122, 136, 141, 164, 174, 190, 195) — the established, existing convention this fix aligns with.
- `tests/bin-lib/exit-code-conformance.test.js` (#1903): the existing mechanical scan, scoped to each file's own entry-point guard only — unchanged by this spec except for the new scoped rule addition.

## Deliverables

- [ ] `churn-report.js`: replace both `process.exit(2)`/`process.exit(1)` calls with `return 2;`/`return 1;` (function falls through with no return / `return undefined` on success, matching every other path's implicit success today).
- [ ] `mark.js`: replace `process.exit(2)` with `return 2;`.
- [ ] `retry-cli.js`'s `update` function: replace both `process.exit(2)`/`process.exit(1)` with `return 2;`/`return 1;`.
- [ ] Update each of the four CLIs' `main()` dispatch lines for `churn-report`, `mark` (the 3 CLIs that have it), and `retry-queue update` (all 4) to capture the returned value and set `process.exitCode` when truthy, e.g.: `if (cmd === 'churn-report') { const code = cmdChurnReport(args); if (code) process.exitCode = code; return; }` — mirror the exact `process.exitCode = N; return;` shape already used by every neighboring branch in the same `main()`.
- [ ] Add a scoped rule to `tests/bin-lib/exit-code-conformance.test.js` (or a small sibling test): no file matching `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/*.js` may contain a `process.exit(` call — sweep the directory's files directly (not call-graph-aware; a flat per-file text scan, same mechanism style as the existing conformance test).
- [ ] Document the scoped rule and its rationale (health-core files are invoked from a caller's own guard, not their own — direct `process.exit()` there bypasses the guard's write-then-flush ordering) in `gh-api-module-pattern/SKILL.md`'s CLI wrapper contract section, alongside the existing guard rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. None of `churn-report.js`, `mark.js`, `retry-cli.js` call `process.exit()` anywhere — verified by the new scoped conformance-test rule.
2. Each of the four health-suite CLIs' `main()` sets `process.exitCode` correctly on every path previously reached via the now-removed `process.exit()` calls — verified by a test invoking each affected command (`churn-report --fail-on-high-churn`, `mark` with a bad status, `retry-queue update` with a missing/malformed file) via the CLI's `main()` and asserting `process.exitCode` (not a subprocess exit code, since these are in-process function calls in the test) equals the previously-hardcoded exit code.
3. The new scoped rule is proven to go red: a synthetic health-core file containing `process.exit(` fails the check; the current health-core directory (post-fix) passes.
4. `gh-api-module-pattern/SKILL.md` documents the scoped rule.
5. `npm test` passes in full, no regressions.

## Technical Approach

Mirror the existing `process.exitCode = N; return;` convention already used throughout all four CLIs' `main()` functions rather than introducing a new signaling shape — the three library functions become ordinary value-returning functions (return a numeric code or `undefined`), and each caller applies that value to `process.exitCode` exactly like every other branch already does. The scoped conformance-test addition is a flat directory sweep (`plugin/bin/lib/health-core/*.js`, checked for the literal `process.exit(` substring/regex, same class of check `#1903`'s existing test already performs), not a call-graph walk — kept simple because the failure class here doesn't need more than "these specific shared files must never exit directly."

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/churn-report.js`, `mark.js`, `retry-cli.js` — the three fixes
- `plugin/bin/code-health.js`, `harness-health.js`, `journey-health.js`, `docs-health.js` — `main()` dispatch line updates
- `tests/bin-lib/exit-code-conformance.test.js` — new scoped rule
- `plugin/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/SKILL.md` — documents the new rule

## Gotchas

- `churn-report.js`'s two exit paths return different codes (2 for a usage error, 1 for the threshold-exceeded case) — preserve both exact values when converting to `return`.
- `code-health.js` has no `mark` command (confirmed: `cmdMark` is not required/dispatched there) — only fix the three CLIs that actually have it (`harness-health.js`, `journey-health.js`, `docs-health.js`).
- Do not widen the new scoped rule to all of `plugin/bin/lib/**` — `statusline-wrapper-source.js`'s own `process.exit()` calls are legitimate (guard-less whole-script, not a library function invoked from another file's guard) and already covered by #1903's existing mechanism; widening the rule would require inventing a new exemption for a file that doesn't actually need one under the narrower scope.

## Original request

## Current State

`plugin/skills/gh-api-module-pattern/SKILL.md`'s CLI wrapper contract documents the `require.main === module` guard rule (`process.exitCode = ...`, never `process.exit()` directly) because `process.exit()` immediately after a pending stdout write can truncate that write for a piped consumer. #1903 just added `tests/bin-lib/exit-code-conformance.test.js`, a mechanical scan for this pattern -- but by design it scopes only to each file's own `require.main === module` entry-point guard (or a guard-less file with no `module.exports`, treated as the whole script). It deliberately does not follow the call graph into library functions a guard invokes.

Three `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/*.js` library files (shared across the four health-suite CLIs -- `code-health.js`, `harness-health.js`, `journey-health.js`, `docs-health.js`) each export a function that calls `process.exit()` directly after a stdout or stderr write, invoked from deep inside those CLIs' own (correctly-written) `main()` flow -- outside any entry-point guard, so `#1903`'s new test cannot see them:

- `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/churn-report.js` line 47: `process.stdout.write(...); process.exit(1);` -- writes a churn table to stdout, then exits immediately when the `--fail-on-high-churn` threshold is exceeded. Line 23 has the same pattern on the stderr usage-error path (`process.exit(2)`).
- `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/mark.js` line 36: `process.stderr.write(...); process.exit(2);` on a usage error.
- `plugin/bin/lib/health-core/retry-cli.js` lines 29 and 36: same stderr-then-exit pattern on two usage-error paths.

This is exactly the class of bug #1176/#1313/#1535/#1903 have been closing one instance at a time -- just one level removed from the guard itself, in a spot the new mechanical check's scope (by design, per its own record's literal deliverable text) does not reach.

## Deliverables

- Decide whether the mechanical check's scope should extend to library functions invoked from an entry-point guard (a call-graph-aware check), or whether these three call sites should instead be fixed directly (buffer the output and return a value for the guard to act on, e.g. `process.exitCode = ...` in the CLI's own `main()`, rather than exiting deep inside the library function) -- a product/design call on how far the mechanical check's contract should reach.
- Whichever direction is chosen, fix the three call sites (`churn-report.js:23,47`, `mark.js:36`, `retry-cli.js:29,36`) so they no longer call `process.exit()` after a pending write.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. None of `churn-report.js`, `mark.js`, `retry-cli.js` call `process.exit()` after a stdout/stderr write reachable from any of the four health-suite CLIs' own entry-point guard.
2. Whatever mechanical or manual check is chosen to prevent recurrence is documented in `gh-api-module-pattern/SKILL.md` or a follow-up to `exit-code-conformance.test.js`.
3. `npm test` passes in full.

## Origin

Surfaced during #1903's own review pass (`/claude-tweaks:review`, worktree `worktree-record-1903`) while verifying the new conformance test's scope against a full `grep -rn "process.exit(" plugin/bin` sweep -- not a finding against #1903's own diff (these three files are untouched by it), so filed as backlog rather than fixed inline.

**Status update from filing time:** the original record's own blocker ("the probe cannot run inside this build — its own subagents are dispatched under the pre-change installed plugin, 6.116.0") is now stale. This session's own read of `subagent-stop.js` confirms the fallback-removal fix has already shipped in the currently installed build (6.118.0). The empirical probe below can run now, in an ordinary `/claude-tweaks:dispatch` or any Task-tool dispatch under the current plugin.

**Complexity:** Low
**Estimated tasks:** 2 (a single blocking empirical Task 0, plus its conditional follow-up)

## Non-Goals

- Speculative code changes to `subagent-stop.js` before the probe result is known — the record's own "Why no code change" section already states correctly that a `source` field reading `agent_transcript_path` alone (the only value it could ever hold post-#1928) proves nothing about harness behavior. Do not add one as a substitute for the actual observation.
- Investigating or fixing `claude-code#27755` (SubagentStop firing unreliably for Task dispatches) directly — it's a harness issue, not this plugin's code; this spec only accounts for it methodologically in Task 0's dispatch count (below), it doesn't attempt to fix it.

## Current State

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` (~line 12, ~line 110): `const transcriptPath = ctx.input.agent_transcript_path;` — no fallback. The file's own header comment confirms the fallback removal already shipped as part of #1928.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` (~line 26): `STATUS_RE` — the exact regex a dispatched agent's first reply line must match to be considered compliant: an optional `- ` bullet prefix, an optional bold `**Status:** ` label, then one of `DONE`, `DONE_WITH_CONCERNS`, `NEEDS_CONTEXT`, `BLOCKED`. Task 0's probe subagent must reply with a first line that matches NONE of these shapes, to deliberately trigger a contract violation if the check is actually live.
- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` (~line 116): `ctxLib.appendEvent(ownedRun.dir, 'contract-violation', { firstLine: trimmedText.split('\n')[0].slice(0, 120) }, ownedRun.attribution)` — the event this Task 0 checks for, written to the owning run's `events.jsonl`.
- The file's own header cites `claude-code#27755`: SubagentStop fires unreliably for Task dispatches — a confound Task 0's dispatch count must account for (a single non-firing dispatch is ambiguous between "hook didn't fire at all" and "hook fired, `agent_transcript_path` absent, check no-op'd").

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Task 0 (blocking, empirical):** dispatch at least 3 independent Task-tool subagents (mitigating the `claude-code#27755` firing-unreliability confound — a single dispatch's silence is ambiguous, three independent silences are stronger evidence), each instructed to reply with a first line that clearly violates `STATUS_RE` (e.g. plain prose with no status word, or a status word buried mid-sentence rather than at the start). Immediately after each dispatch completes, read that run's `events.jsonl` and check for a `contract-violation` event.
- [ ] Record the literal observed result verbatim in this spec's own `## Gotchas` before considering this closed: how many of the 3+ dispatches produced a `contract-violation` event, and (if any did) whether the event's `firstLine` matches the deliberately-violating reply — confirming the check fired for the right reason, not a coincidental unrelated log line.
- [ ] **Conditional on zero violations detected across all dispatches:** file this as a new, separate finding (not fixed inline in this spec) — `agent_transcript_path` is not delivered by the harness in this environment, and `subagent-stop.js`'s E3 check needs a different input signal entirely. Do not guess at what that signal should be here; that's a new design question for a follow-up record.
- [ ] **Conditional on at least one violation detected:** close this spec as confirmed-working — the check is live, no code change needed. State this plainly rather than treating "we found nothing wrong" as an unsatisfying result; a clean confirmation is exactly what this spec exists to produce.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. At least 3 independent Task-tool dispatches were made, each with a reply deliberately violating `STATUS_RE`.
2. Each dispatch's owning run's `events.jsonl` was checked for a `contract-violation` event, and the count of dispatches that did/did not produce one is stated exactly (e.g. "3 of 3", "0 of 3", "1 of 3") — not rounded to "some"/"most".
3. The literal observed result is recorded in this spec's `## Gotchas` (or, once resolved, in the closing PR/commit description) before this record closes.
4. If zero violations were detected, a new record is filed via `/claude-tweaks:capture` naming the confirmed gap and proposing the next investigation step (what alternative input signal might work) — not fixed inline here.

## Technical Approach

No code changes are anticipated unless Task 0 confirms the check is inert, in which case the conditional deliverable routes to a new record rather than expanding this spec's own scope. This keeps the empirical result and any resulting design work cleanly separated — this spec's only job is to produce the observation.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` — read-only reference for `STATUS_RE` and the `contract-violation` event shape; no edits anticipated here
- `{owning run directory}/events.jsonl` — read target for Task 0's check, path varies per dispatch

## Gotchas

- {Task 0's literal observed result goes here once run: N of 3+ dispatches produced a contract-violation event, and whether each event's firstLine matched the deliberately-violating reply.}
- Do not add a `source` field to the `contract-violation` event as a substitute for running Task 0 — the record's own original analysis (preserved below) already explains why that would prove nothing under the current code.
- `claude-code#27755` means a single non-firing dispatch is not conclusive on its own — Task 0's 3+ dispatch count exists specifically to distinguish "harness didn't fire the hook this one time" from "hook fired but the field was absent."

## Original request

# #1928 leftover — is the SubagentStop status-line check now silently inert?

**What changed:** `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` no longer falls back to the parent session's `transcript_path` when `agent_transcript_path` is absent (spec Deliverable 5, AC5). The whole-branch review sampled 1,887 archived `contract-violation` events — every one was orchestrator narration graded through that fallback; none carried an agent-scoped transcript.

**What is not proven:** nothing in the corpus shows `agent_transcript_path` ever being populated by the harness. If it is not, the check is now a no-op and nobody would notice — the event payload records no transcript source, so absence of events is indistinguishable from "every agent complied".

**Why no code change in this run:** a `source` field on the event would only ever read `agent_transcript_path` now (the fallback is gone), so it proves nothing about the harness; the only evidence is one observed true positive after this ships.

**Proposed console action:** file a follow-up record via `/claude-tweaks:capture` — "After #1928 ships, dispatch one subagent whose reply deliberately omits the status line and confirm a `contract-violation` event lands in the owning run's `events.jsonl`; if none does, `agent_transcript_path` is not delivered by the harness and the check needs a different input." `Defer-reason: needs-live-observation` — the probe cannot run inside this build (its own subagents are dispatched under the pre-change installed plugin, 6.116.0).

Surface: infra

## Current State

`plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` (E3, warn tier) reads the stopping subagent's transcript, exempts third-party `agent_type`s (#1596), and on a missing status line appends one `contract-violation` event to the owning run's `events.jsonl`; its header states "Never blocks" and that the event fires unreliably for Task dispatches (claude-code#27755). On a violation it returns a warn-tier `systemMessage` naming the missing status line; on every other path it returns `{}`. `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` registers it under `SubagentStop`. `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` documents the hook as best-effort logging and tells the dispatcher to re-prompt by hand. #1596 (closed) shipped the exemption and a stronger dispatch template and deferred in-run enforcement because two lookups of the Claude Code hooks reference disagreed on whether `SubagentStop` accepts a blocking decision.

Lead, not yet the answer: the hooks reference (`https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks`, read 2026-09-09) lists `SubagentStop` in its exit-code-2 table as "Prevents the subagent from stopping" and describes a `hookSpecificOutput` block with a `blockSubagentStop`-style flag and reason field; `permissionDecision` is documented for the tool events only, so the field names #1596 tested were the wrong ones. The exact field names and whether the blocked subagent actually continues must be captured from a live run, not from a summary. #1868 (open, `needs:definition`) holds the wider "which enforcement point" question for status-word violations; this record is the mechanical probe that decides whether the hook-side option is available at all.

Tests: `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` pins the contract prose; `subagent-stop.js`'s exemption logic is tested with fake `ctx` objects in `tests/hooks-log-modules.test.js`.

## Deliverables

- [ ] **Task 0 — empirical premise check (blocking).** Dispatch one throwaway Task subagent whose prompt makes its first line deliberately narrative, with a temporary `subagent-stop.js` variant that returns the documented blocking output (try, in order, `hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: 'SubagentStop', blockSubagentStop: true, blockSubagentStopReason: … }`, then the `decision: 'block'` + `reason` shape, then exit code 2). Capture verbatim: the hook's stdin payload field names, the output that worked, and the subagent's transcript showing whether it continued and re-replied. Mandatory teardown: restore `subagent-stop.js` unconditionally, delete the throwaway transcript, and confirm no `contract-violation` event from the probe remains in any live run dir. Record the literal captured behavior in `subagent-stop.js`'s header comment and in this issue.
- [ ] **If supported: forced retry with a one-retry cap.** On a violation from a non-exempt `agent_type`, return the blocking output with a reason that quotes the contract's status-line rule and the offending first line; count retries per `(session_id, agent_id)` in `${os.tmpdir()}/ct-contract-retries-${sessionId}.json` (the `resolve-profile.js` blacklist-file convention); on the second violation of the same agent, log the event as today and let it stop. A failed counter write counts as "already retried" so a broken tmp dir can never loop. Update the header comment's "Never blocks" sentence and `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`'s E3 paragraph and Anti-Patterns to describe the one forced retry; `docs/hooks.md` gains one sentence naming the tier change (warn → one-shot block).
- [ ] **If unsupported: close with the limitation recorded**, and file one follow-up under #1868 proposing the dispatcher-facing alternative (surfacing `contract-violation` via `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` on a dispatcher-side event) so the definition there has the evidence.
- [ ] **Tests (supported branch).** Fake-`ctx` cases beside the existing exemption tests: first violation → blocking output with the reason; second violation same `(session_id, agent_id)` → `{}` plus the logged event; exempt `agent_type` → `{}` with no counter write; counter write throwing → treated as already retried; a compliant reply → `{}` and no counter file. `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` updated for the revised E3 clause.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `subagent-stop.js`'s header comment and this issue carry the Task 0 capture: the exact input field names observed, the exact output shape that blocked (or the evidence that none did), and the transcript excerpt showing the subagent's behavior after the block.
2. Supported branch: a non-exempt violating subagent is blocked exactly once per `(session_id, agent_id)`; the second violation stops normally with the event logged; exempt agents are never blocked; the probe's teardown left no plugin file modified (`git status` clean on `plugin/`).
3. Unsupported branch: this record is closed with the captured evidence and one follow-up record exists under #1868 naming the dispatcher-facing alternative.
4. `npm test` green; the existing exemption tests pass unchanged.
5. `_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`, `docs/hooks.md`, and the hook's header agree on the tier (one forced retry, or warn-only with the limitation named).

## Technical Approach

Probe before code, per `spec-template.md`'s Empirical Premise-Check Deliverables: the doc lead above is a hypothesis with field names from a summary, and the hook's own history (#1928, claude-code#27755) shows this event's behavior drifts. Keep the block one-shot and counter-backed so the never-break-a-session invariant holds even when the harness re-fires the event; keep the exemption check first so third-party agents never see a block. The wider enforcement-point decision stays with #1868; this record only settles whether the hook-side option exists and, if so, ships its minimal form.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` — Task 0 capture in the header; blocking output; retry counter
- `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md` — E3 paragraph and Anti-Patterns
- `docs/hooks.md` — tier sentence
- `tests/hooks-log-modules.test.js` (fake-`ctx` hook cases) and `tests/subagent-contract-clauses.test.js` — new cases

## Gotchas

- The probe mutates a hook that fires for every subagent in the session; run it in an isolated worktree session with the plugin loaded from that checkout (`claude --plugin-dir ./plugin`), never against the installed build.
- `SubagentStop` "fires unreliably for Task dispatches" (claude-code#27755): a probe that sees no event at all is inconclusive, not "unsupported"; repeat once before concluding.
- The counter file is per session; a blocked subagent that is re-dispatched with a new `agent_id` is a new agent by design.
- Never block on an absent `agent_transcript_path` (#1928's fix): no transcript means no evidence, and the hook must still return `{}` there.

## Original request

# In-run enforcement follow-up from #1596

**Origin:** #1596 build (deferred, scope-down decision — see that record's Blocked / Future Work section and its materialized spec at `.claude-tweaks/pipelines/2026-09-05T174526-record-1596/work/1596-spec.md`)

## Current State

#1596 shipped an `agent_type` exemption fix to `plugin/bin/lib/hooks/subagent-stop.js` and a
strengthened dispatch template in `plugin/skills/_shared/subagent-output-contract.md`, but did not
implement forcing a violating subagent to retry in-run via the `SubagentStop` hook's own
decision-control output. Whether `SubagentStop`'s JSON output actually supports
`permissionDecision: "block"` / `permissionDecisionReason` (the way `Stop`'s documented decision
control does) was not confirmed within that build's investigation budget — two lookups against
Claude Code's own hooks reference (`https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks`) disagreed, and the
session hit a rate limit before a third, decisive lookup could run.

## Deliverables

- Resolve the platform-support question definitively: a live probe (dispatch one throwaway Task
  subagent whose reply is deliberately malformed, have `subagent-stop.js` attempt the
  `permissionDecision: 'block'` response, and confirm from the subagent's own transcript/behavior
  whether it was actually forced to continue rather than stopping) before implementing the
  forced-retry mechanism either way.
- If confirmed supported: implement the forced-retry mechanism in `subagent-stop.js`, scoped to
  non-exempt `agent_type`s only (reuse #1596's exemption check), with a one-retry cap per
  `(session_id, agent_id)` — mirror `resolve-profile.js`'s session-scoped model-failure-blacklist
  convention (`${os.tmpdir()}/ct-model-failures-${sessionId}.json`) for the retry-count file
  (`${os.tmpdir()}/ct-contract-retries-${sessionId}.json`), to avoid an infinite retry loop if the
  write itself fails.
- If confirmed unsupported: close this record noting the platform limitation, and consider
  whether `friction-events.js`'s existing `contract-violation` detection could instead be surfaced
  back to the *dispatching* agent in-run some other way (e.g. via `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`
  on a different, dispatcher-facing hook event) rather than acting on the violating subagent itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A definitive, sourced answer to "does `SubagentStop`'s JSON output support a blocking decision
   field," recorded in this issue or in `subagent-stop.js`'s own comments.
2. If yes: a working forced-retry implementation with a one-retry cap, tested the same way
   #1596's `tests/hooks-subagent-stop.test.js` tests its exemption logic (fake `ctx` objects, no
   live harness dependency).

Surface: backend

## Overview

`flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s "Auto-resolution short-circuit" section still carries a hand-rolled per-item resolution procedure (render every section as `AUTO-RESOLVED`, resolve every item per its stated default, log one decisions line per item, write no `console.json`) — the same shape `wrap-up/review-console.md`'s single-spec short-circuit had before #1932 replaced it with one `console-resolve.js --run … --policy console-auto` call. The two consoles' unattended paths have drifted structurally since, and the multi-spec path's missing `console.json` write leaves an unattended multi-spec run un-archived by `archive-merged.js`'s `readConsoleState` — the same problem #1854 fixed for the single-spec path.

**Design resolved before shaping (the record's own open Deliverables choice):** `console-resolve.js`'s CLI (`plugin/bin/console-resolve.js` ~line 45, 109-110) accepts exactly one `--run <dir>` per invocation, and `bin/lib/console/resolve.js`'s `readSnapshot`/`readMembers` (~lines 101-144) read a single flat run dir's own `work/`, `staged/`, `decisions.md`, `engine-state.json` directly — there is no parent-manifest-aware mode and none should be added here (that would duplicate the multi-spec file's own existing manifest-reading logic in a second place). Since each `spec-{N}/` subdirectory already has exactly that single-run-dir shape, and the multi-spec console's own Step 2 (unchanged by this spec) already reads the parent run dir's own `decisions.md`/`staged/` as a separate unit from each spec's, the correct call pattern is: **once per `spec-{N}/` directory, plus once more over the parent run dir itself** — never a single call over the whole tree.

**Complexity:** Medium
**Estimated tasks:** 3-4

## Non-Goals

- Adding parent-manifest-awareness to `bin/lib/console/resolve.js` itself (a `readMembers`/`readSnapshot` mode that walks `spec-*/` subdirectories in one call) — rejected above; would duplicate logic the multi-spec skill file already owns.
- Changing the single-spec `wrap-up/review-console.md` short-circuit (#1932's already-shipped call) in any way.
- Changing the bundle-level branch-finish/merge decision's own carve-out logic (needs-human, ungranted-member — both already documented in the file's existing "Auto-resolution short-circuit" prose) — see Gotchas below for why each `console-resolve.js` call's own per-spec `merge.resolution` field must NOT be wired into that bundle-level decision.

## Current State

- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md` (~line 66), "Auto-resolution short-circuit" section: per-item resolution loop, `AUTO-RESOLVED` stamping, per-item decisions-line logging — all hand-rolled, structurally diverged from the single-spec file's one-call approach.
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` (~line 91): the single-spec precedent this record asks to mirror — `console-resolve.js --run "$PIPELINE_RUN_DIR" --policy console-auto`, one decisions block, one `console.json`, one rendered table, then routes every returned resolution through the file's own "On approval" procedure.
- `plugin/bin/console-resolve.js`: `--run <dir>` is single-valued and required (~line 45); `--run` must resolve to a directory anchored under the main checkout (~line 111-113) or the call refuses.
- `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js`: `readMembers` (~line 103) and `readSnapshot` (~line 124) both operate on one `runDir` — `work/*.md`, `staged/`, `decisions.md`, `engine-state.json` directly inside it.
- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s own Step 3 (~line 24-30) already establishes the precedent for graceful per-spec failure isolation across a multi-call fan-out: when `wrap-up-engine.js`'s one combined `--spec-state` call fails for a malformed spec, "drop only the offending spec's `--spec-state` flag and re-run... Note the dropped spec in the console's Not run/Failed footer with the CLI's own error text as the reason" — this spec's `console-resolve.js` fan-out should follow the same isolation pattern, not let one bad spec abort the whole short-circuit.
- `tests/console-resolve-conformance.test.js`: the existing pin for the single-spec file's one-call shape — the template this spec's new test mirrors.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Replace `multispec-review-console.md`'s "Auto-resolution short-circuit" per-item loop with a fan-out: for each `spec-{N}/` directory (manifest order, from Step 1's `manifest.yml` read) plus the parent run dir itself, invoke `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/console-resolve.js" --run {dir} --policy console-auto` (append `--dry-run` when the run itself is `--dry-run`).
- [ ] A call that exits non-zero for one `spec-{N}/` (malformed `engine-state.json` or similar) does not abort the fan-out for the rest — isolate it per the existing Step 3 precedent (Current State above): note the dropped spec in the Not run/Failed footer with the CLI's own error text, continue with the remaining calls.
- [ ] Aggregate every call's rendered table into the consolidated console (one render per spec-dir plus the parent's, in manifest order) — same "insert stdout verbatim, do not hand-expand" rule Step 3 already states for the engine call.
- [ ] Compute the bundle-level branch-finish/merge decision exactly as the section's existing carve-out prose already does (needs-human verdict, ungranted-member) — do NOT read or use any individual `console-resolve.js` call's own `merge.resolution` field for this; each call's merge computation is per-single-spec-dir and has no visibility into the bundle's other members, so it cannot correctly decide a shared branch-finish. State this explicitly in the section's prose so a future edit doesn't wire it in by mistake.
- [ ] A conformance test (new, or added to `tests/console-resolve-conformance.test.js`) pins: the multi-spec file's short-circuit section contains `console-resolve.js" --run` and no per-item `AUTO-RESOLVED` resolution loop remains; the fan-out iterates spec dirs plus the parent (not a single call over the whole tree).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s Auto-resolution short-circuit section contains `console-resolve.js" --run` and no hand-rolled per-item resolution loop — verified by the new conformance test, proven to go red against a frozen pre-change excerpt of the current per-item-loop prose (`skill-prose-conformance-tests` convention).
2. An unattended multi-spec run leaves `console.json` under each `spec-{N}/` directory AND under the parent run dir — both readable by `archive-merged.js`'s `readConsoleState`.
3. One spec's `console-resolve.js` call failing does not silently drop the whole console — the affected spec appears in the Not run/Failed footer, the rest resolve normally — verified by a test simulating one malformed `engine-state.json` among several valid spec dirs.
4. The bundle-level merge/branch-finish decision is computed by the section's existing carve-out logic only, never by any per-call `merge.resolution` field — verified by a test asserting the prose states this explicitly (a doesNotMatch-style pin proving the wiring isn't silently introduced).
5. `npm test` passes with no regressions.

## Technical Approach

Mirror `wrap-up/review-console.md`'s already-shipped one-call pattern (#1932), extended to N+1 calls (one per spec dir, one for the parent) rather than one call over a hypothetical parent-aware mode — because `console-resolve.js`'s `--run` is single-directory by construction, adding parent-awareness to the resolver itself would duplicate logic the multi-spec skill file already owns for reading per-spec directories (Step 1's manifest read). Failure isolation across the fan-out reuses the file's own existing precedent from Step 3's engine call rather than inventing a new pattern.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/flow/multispec-review-console.md` — the Auto-resolution short-circuit section (~line 66) is what changes
- `plugin/bin/console-resolve.js` / `plugin/bin/lib/console/resolve.js` — reference only, no changes anticipated
- `tests/console-resolve-conformance.test.js` — template/extension point for the new conformance test

## Gotchas

- Do not add a parent-manifest-aware mode to `bin/lib/console/resolve.js` — rejected in Non-Goals; the multi-spec skill file already owns manifest-reading, and duplicating it in the resolver creates two places that can drift.
- The bundle-level merge decision is genuinely NOT the same computation as any single spec's `console-resolve.js` call — each call only sees its own spec dir's grants/verdicts, never the bundle's other members. Wiring a per-call `merge.resolution` into the bundle decision would silently break the existing needs-human/ungranted-member carve-outs, which are computed across ALL members. This is the one correctness risk in this spec that the original record's Deliverables didn't call out at all — flagged explicitly so the implementer doesn't introduce it.
- Mirror Step 3's existing per-spec failure-isolation precedent (Current State above) for the fan-out — don't let one malformed spec dir abort the whole console.

## Original request

# Route the multi-spec Review Console's short-circuit through console-resolve.js

**Current State:** #1932 replaced `wrap-up/review-console.md`'s per-item `consoleAutoResolve` loop with one `console-resolve.js --run … --policy console-auto` call (one decisions block, one `console.json`, one table). `flow/multispec-review-console.md` (~line 66) still carries its own per-item resolution loop for the consolidated multi-spec console, so the two consoles' unattended paths are now structurally different and will drift — the multi-spec one has no `console.json` write either, so a merged multi-spec unattended run stays un-archived for the same reason #1854 named.

**Deliverables:**
- `flow/multispec-review-console.md`'s short-circuit calls `console-resolve.js` once per spec run dir (or once over the parent with per-spec items, whichever the resolver's member model supports — decide at plan time against `bin/lib/console/resolve.js`'s `readMembers`), renders the returned tables, executes resolutions per the same resolution→step map.
- The resolver handles a parent multi-spec run dir (manifest ids, `spec-*/staged/`), or the prose runs it per spec dir — one of the two, stated.
- A conformance test pins the multi-spec file's single call and exit-code routing like `tests/console-resolve-conformance.test.js` does for the single-spec file.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
1. `flow/multispec-review-console.md` contains `console-resolve.js" --run` exactly once and no per-item resolution loop.
2. An unattended multi-spec run leaves `console.json` under each spec dir (or the parent), readable by `archive-merged.js`'s `readConsoleState`.
3. `npm test` passes with no new failures.

Defer-reason: out of #1932's Non-Goals ("Any interactive console change" / the multi-spec console was not in scope) — surfaced by #1932's whole-branch review (M8).

Surface: backend

**Related:** #1987, #2019

## Overview

Bring the composed `merge` bundle (`_shared/pr-first-merge.md` + `_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`, read by `/wrap-up`'s two pr-first merge sites via `bin/compose-context.js`) under the 40 KB composed-bytes ceiling `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js` now enforces per compose call site, and remove the `merge` entry from `COMPOSED_STEP_EXCEPTIONS`.

## Current State

- #1989 fenced the two sources' branch-specific prose with `when:` markers without rewriting a sentence. Under `integration-model=pr-first` + `transport=gh` the composed bundle measures 55,995 B (raw sources 58,612 B): additive fencing of prose that already exists saved 4.5%, because almost all of both files is genuinely pr-first-and-gh procedure.
- #1990 added the composed-bytes hard gate. The `merge` step is the only real call site and is over the ceiling under every combination — 55,995 B (pr-first+gh), 57,476 (pr-first+mcp), 57,274 (local-merge+gh), 58,755 (local-merge+mcp), 58,761 (both branches, the standalone-run read) — so the gate carries `COMPOSED_STEP_EXCEPTIONS = { merge: 59 * 1024 }` — a provisional per-step ceiling 1,655 B above the measured maximum, pinned to at most 4 KiB of slack by the stale-exception test, that fails on any growth, with a stale-exception test that fails the moment the step fits under `CEILING_BYTES`. Parent #1987's Cross-Spec Promise F4 records the byte figures.
- Both `/wrap-up` merge sites fall back to reading the two sources directly when the compose command is unavailable, so the both-branches read (58,612 B) is what a standalone run pays today.

## Deliverables

- [ ] Measure which sections of the two sources a merge-time reader actually needs at the moment of `gh pr merge` (the Step 2.5 gate, Step 3's merge attempt and its degrade chain, the post-merge handoff) versus what is run-start or phase-checklist procedure already executed by then (`pr-early-run-lifecycle.md`'s Steps 1-4 open the draft PR at run start) — a per-section reader-need table, cited from the sites that read each section.
- [ ] Narrow the `merge` call site's source list or split `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` along the reader-need boundary (a lazily-read sub-file for the run-start half, per `docs/skill-authoring.md`'s composition-over-fragmentation rule: a split is legitimate only when some reads never need the other half), so that every `integration-model` × `transport` combination composes under `CEILING_BYTES`; byte-identity of the moved prose proven (`stripMarkers` vs `git show origin/main`).
- [ ] Remove `merge` from `COMPOSED_STEP_EXCEPTIONS`; the stale-exception test and the hard gate both pass on the real corpus with no exception.
- [ ] Update `docs/skill-graph.md`'s `_shared/pr-first-merge.md` row and the `#1989` journey step (`docs/journeys/compose-a-per-run-context-bundle-1988.md` step 6) to the new source list; flip promise F4 on #1987 to satisfied.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `node --test tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` passes with `COMPOSED_STEP_EXCEPTIONS` empty.
2. The informational composed-bytes table shows every `merge` combination at or under 40,960 B.
3. Every citer of a moved section still resolves (grep for the section headings and anchors across `plugin/skills/**` and `docs/**`).
4. `npm test` passes.

## Non-Goals

- Raising `CEILING_BYTES` — the parent design fixes it at the number a reader pays per step.
- Rewriting the merge procedure's semantics; only where prose lives and which sources the call site names change.

## Technical Approach

Measure before moving: the reader-need table is the deliverable that decides between the two mechanisms, and it is built from the two call sites that read the bundle (`wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md`'s composed read and the Review Console's merge path), not from the sources' own headings. Prefer narrowing the call site's source list when the run-start half is never needed at merge time; split `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` only if some merge-time reads need part of it, and then move prose byte-identically (`stripMarkers` output compared against `git show origin/main:{path}`) so the `when:` fencing from #1989 keeps its meaning. Remove the exception last, so the stale-exception test flips from "exception too generous" to "no exception needed" in the same commit that makes it true.

### Key Files

- `plugin/bin/lib/skill-audit/context-cost.js` — remove the `merge` entry from `COMPOSED_STEP_EXCEPTIONS`
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/auto-merge-short-circuit.md` — the `merge` compose call site: its `compose-context.js --step merge {sources}` argv is the source list to narrow or repoint (the composer takes sources from argv; `context-cost.js` measures call sites found in skill prose)
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` — run-start half split out only if the reader-need table justifies it
- `plugin/skills/_shared/pr-first-merge.md` — citations to any moved section
- `plugin/skills/wrap-up/review-console.md` — the second merge-path reader and its direct-read fallback
- `docs/skill-graph.md`, `docs/journeys/compose-a-per-run-context-bundle-1988.md` — source-list rows and journey step 6
- `tests/bin-lib/skill-audit/context-cost.test.js` — passes with an empty exception map

## Gotchas

- Sources today: `pr-first-merge.md` 30,404 B and `pr-early-run-lifecycle.md` 30,181 B; the ceiling is 40,960 B composed, so narrowing alone works only if the merge-time reader needs strictly less than about two thirds of the pair.
- The direct-read fallback (compose command unavailable) must land under the ceiling too, or a standalone run keeps paying the both-branches read; the AC's "every combination" includes it.
- #1987 is closed; flipping promise F4 is an edit to that record's body, not a reopen.
- #2019 (open) proposes section-scoped review/test bundles after this restructuring; do not pre-empt its scope here.

## Current State

Record #1302 built the WEBHOOK-TRIGGER mode (`plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md`), the `webhook_triggers` schema field, the filter grammar, and both preconditions -- all documented from `create_webhook_trigger`'s own tool description, since `RemoteTrigger` was confirmed unavailable via `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in that build session. This is the 4th consecutive session (2026-08-23 x2, 2026-08-26, 2026-09-05) to confirm the same unavailability. AC2 ("verified against a real (or explicitly documented dry-run) call") remains unmet: the request/response shape has never actually been confirmed against a live `create_webhook_trigger` call.

A prior follow-up for this same gap, #1485, was filed and closed on 2026-08-31 -- but the closing commit (`e0d4aded`, "[fast-lane] Dispatch-queue, worktree-guard, reconcile, and process-hygiene fixes (19 records)") bundled 19 unrelated record numbers via `Fixes #N` and contains no work touching `webhook-trigger.md`, `RemoteTrigger`, or live-call verification. #1485 appears to have been swept into an unrelated batch closure rather than substantively resolved -- its own acceptance criterion (a live or explicit-dry-run `create_webhook_trigger` call) was never actually satisfied. This record exists so the gap is not lost a second time to the same failure mode; whoever picks this up should close it only against real evidence of a live (or explicit dry-run) call, not a batch commit that doesn't mention the file.

## Deliverables

- Re-run `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in a session where the tool may be reachable -- 4 consecutive interactive-session misses is a strong signal worth testing in a different session type (cloud/routine) if one becomes available.
- Once reachable, call `create_webhook_trigger` against a real (or an explicit, logged dry-run) routine and record its actual required fields, response shape, and any App-not-installed error text.
- Diff the actual response against what `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md` currently documents (Step 5's assembled body, the `routine_trigger_id` field, the App-not-installed error detection) and correct any mismatch.
- Before closing, verify the closing commit/PR actually touches `webhook-trigger.md` or names the live-verification evidence directly -- do not let this close via an unrelated batch sweep the way #1485 did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A live (or explicit dry-run) `create_webhook_trigger` call has been made and its actual request/response shape is confirmed to match (or has been corrected to match) `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md`.
- The closing commit or PR description names this evidence directly (a transcript excerpt, a diff to `webhook-trigger.md`, or an explicit "confirmed matching, no changes needed" note) rather than a bare `Fixes #N` in an unrelated batch.

## Technical Approach

Start with `ToolSearch select:RemoteTrigger` in whichever session type is available at build time. If reachable, make one real or explicit-dry-run `create_webhook_trigger` call and capture its actual request/response shape verbatim before touching the docs. Then diff that captured shape against `webhook-trigger.md`'s current documentation section by section (assembled body, `routine_trigger_id`, App-not-installed error detection) and correct only what actually differs.

### Key Files

- `plugin/skills/routine/webhook-trigger.md` -- the documented request/response shape to verify and correct

## Gotchas

- If `RemoteTrigger`/`create_webhook_trigger` is still unreachable in whatever session builds this record, do not fabricate a "verified" result and do not close this record -- report the continued unavailability plainly (a 5th consecutive miss is itself a useful data point) and leave it open.
